name: Tamoxifen
mechanism: Competitive oestrogen receptor (ER) antagonist in breast tissue (blocks oestrogen-stimulated tumor growth). Partial ER agonist in bone (maintains density), endometrium (proliferative - ↑ endometrial cancer risk), liver (favourable lipid profile). Metabolized to active metabolites (endoxifen, 4-hydroxytamoxifen - more potent anti-oestrogenic activity)
dosing: Adjuvant breast cancer: 20mg PO OD for 5-10 years (premenopausal ER+ breast cancer). Risk reduction (high-risk): 20mg OD for 5 years. Take at same time daily, with/without food. Longer duration (10 years) may be more beneficial than 5 years in some patients
contraindications: Pregnancy (teratogenic). History of venous thromboembolism (VTE). Concurrent anticoagulation (relative - bleeding risk with endometrial effects). Caution: pre-existing endometrial pathology, thromboembolic risk factors, cataracts, hepatic impairment
interactions: CYP2D6 inhibitors (paroxetine, fluoxetine, bupropion, cinacalcet, duloxetine) ↓ conversion to active endoxifen - reduced efficacy (avoid if possible, use alternative antidepressants like venlafaxine, citalopram). Warfarin: ↑ INR (monitor closely, may need dose adjustment). CYP3A4 inducers (rifampicin) ↓ levels. Oestrogen-containing medications reduce efficacy (avoid HRT)
monitoring: Annual gynaecological review (endometrial thickness, abnormal bleeding - ↑ endometrial cancer risk). Ophthalmology if visual symptoms (cataracts, retinopathy). Signs/symptoms of VTE (leg pain/swelling, breathlessness). LFTs (baseline, periodically - rare hepatotoxicity). Bone density (protective in postmenopausal). Lipid profile (may improve). Adherence (long-term therapy - counsel importance)
pregnancy: CONTRAINDICATED - teratogenic (genital tract abnormalities). Women of childbearing potential: effective contraception (non-hormonal - barrier methods). If pregnancy occurs, stop immediately. Advise to avoid pregnancy during and for 2 months after stopping
sideEffects: Very common: hot flushes (65%), vaginal discharge, menstrual irregularities (premenopausal). Common: nausea, fatigue, mood changes, arthralgia, oedema. Important serious: VTE (DVT, PE - 1-2%), endometrial hyperplasia/cancer (2-3× increased risk - monitor for abnormal bleeding), stroke (small increased risk), cataracts/visual disturbances. Rare: hepatotoxicity, hypercalcaemia (at start if bone metastases), thrombocytopenia
pharmacokinetics: Well absorbed orally. Extensive first-pass metabolism by CYP2D6 (to endoxifen - major active metabolite, 30-100× more potent than tamoxifen) and CYP3A4 (to 4-hydroxytamoxifen). Half-life: 5-7 days (prolonged - once-daily dosing). Enterohepatic recirculation. Steady-state 4-8 weeks. Excreted mainly in faeces. CYP2D6 polymorphisms affect efficacy (poor metabolizers ↓ endoxifen levels - worse outcomes)
clinicalPearls: Pioneering breast cancer therapy (1970s). First-line adjuvant endocrine therapy for premenopausal ER+ breast cancer. Postmenopausal: aromatase inhibitors (letrozole, anastrozole, exemestane) often preferred (more effective, but tamoxifen if AI intolerant/contraindicated). Duration: traditionally 5 years, but ATLAS/aTTom trials showed benefit of 10 years vs 5 (lower recurrence, mortality). Discuss with patient. KEY BENEFIT: ↓ recurrence risk, contralateral breast cancer, mortality. Also used for risk reduction in high-risk women (BRCA, strong family history - ↓ breast cancer incidence by ~40%). KEY RISKS: VTE (especially first 2 years, surgery, immobility - consider thromboprophylaxis perioperatively), endometrial cancer (annual review, investigate any postmenopausal bleeding), hot flushes (challenging - lifestyle, SSRIs/SNRIs but avoid CYP2D6 inhibitors). CYP2D6 inhibitors reduce efficacy: AVOID paroxetine, fluoxetine (strong 2D6 inhibitors). If antidepressant needed (hot flushes, mood), use venlafaxine, citalopram, escitalopram (minimal 2D6 inhibition). CYP2D6 genotyping controversial - not routine, but consider if therapy failure. Hot flush management: lifestyle (layered clothing, fans), non-hormonal (venlafaxine, clonidine, gabapentin). Avoid HRT (oestrogen antagonizes tamoxifen). VTE risk: counsel on leg pain/swelling, breathlessness. Thromboprophylaxis if major surgery. Alternatives postmenopausal: AIs (letrozole, anastrozole) more effective but more arthralgia, osteoporosis. Tamoxifen if AI intolerant. Switch strategies: tamoxifen → AI after 2-3 years (reduced recurrence vs tamoxifen alone). Compliance critical: long-term therapy (5-10 years) - regular review, address side effects
indication: Adjuvant treatment of oestrogen receptor-positive (ER+) breast cancer (especially premenopausal). Risk reduction in high-risk women. Treatment of metastatic breast cancer
